Revendiquée par le Groupe de soutien à l’islam et aux musulmans (JNIM), affilié à Al-Qaïda, l’attaque a été repoussée par les Forces de défense et de sécurité (FDS) après plus de deux heures de violents affrontement

france24fr.title: Un manuscrit inédit de Mozart, petit trésor mis en musique à Paris
france24fr.description: C'est une rare découverte : un cahier de composition de Mozart, sept pièces pour flûte et harpe et des leçons qu'il donnait à la duchesse de Guînes, a été retrouvé grâce à la persévérance d'un conservateur de la Bibliothèque nationale de France (BnF).

france24fr.title: Mondial 2026 : les États-Unis en 16es, le Brésil et le Maroc s'en rapprochent
france24fr.description: Au lendemain de la qualification du Mexique, les États-Unis, autres coorganisateurs du Mondial 2026, ont à leur tour validé vendredi leur billet pour les 16es de finale, dont se rapprochent aussi le Brésil et le Maroc.

france24fr.title: Chaleur : la canicule s'étend, vigilance rouge en vue dimanche
france24fr.description: Oraux du bac perturbés, prudence de mise sur les chantiers et lors de la Fête de la musique : la canicule a continué à s'étendre vendredi 19 juin, avec 53 départements placés en vigilance orange, bientôt 60 samedi, et un niveau "rouge" qui pourrait être déclenché dimanche dans certaines zones.

france24fr.title: Pologne : le président annonce retirer la plus haute distinction du pays à Zelensky
france24fr.description: Le président polonais, Karol Nawrocki, a annoncé vendredi 19 juin qu'il retirait la plus haute distinction du pays au président ukrainien, Volodymyr Zelensky, l'Ordre de l'Aigle blanc, sur fond de tensions liées à l'histoire commune des deux États voisins.

france24fr.title: Frappes au Liban : "Il y a une violation de l'accord signé par Trump et Pezeshkian"
france24fr.description: La rencontre en Suisse avec J.D. Vance pour discuter de l'application de l'accord signé par Trump et Pezeshkian pour mettre fin à la guerre au Moyen-Orient, prévue ce vendredi 19 juin, a été annulée. "Tant que la guerre n'est pas arrêtée au Liban, il n'est pas question de discuter avec les Américains" du côté iranien, rapporte notre correspondant Siavosh Ghazi.

france24fr.title: Europe : comment les crises énergétiques accélèrent les renouvelables
france24fr.description:
🚛💨 En Belgique, des camions sont désormais rechargés grâce à l'énergie du vent stockée dans des batteries.
 
Face aux crises énergétiques et aux tensions géopolitiques, les énergies renouvelables ne sont plus seulement un enjeu climatique : elles deviennent aussi un enjeu de souveraineté énergétique.

france24fr.title: Avec sa Cité internationale, Annecy devient capitale mondiale de l’animation "toute l’année"
france24fr.description: Pendant tout le week-end, Annecy fête l’ouverture de sa toute nouvelle Cité internationale du cinéma d'animation, un projet à 54,5 millions d’euros qui regroupe notamment un musée, des ateliers d'initiation à l'image par image, un cinéma et une résidence d'artistes. Entretien avec la directrice Culture Peggy Zejgman-Lecarme.

spiegel.title: Iran verkündet erneute Schließung der Straße von Hormus
spiegel.description: Der Iran will die Straße von Hormus wieder für Schiffe sperren. Als Grund dafür nennt das zentrale Militärkommando des Landes die Nichteinhaltung der Waffenruhe im Südlibanon, die die USA und der Iran vereinbart hatten.

spiegel.title: Artenschutz-Kontrolle am Flughafen Frankfurt: Eisbär im Gepäck
spiegel.description: Elfenbein, Schlangenhaut, Giraffenfell: Der Zoll bewahrt verbotene Gegenstände aus aller Welt in einem speziellen Raum auf. Wie gelangt die Schmuggelware dorthin? Ein Besuch im Gruselkabinett des Frankfurter Flughafens.

spiegel.title: Die Linke: Luigi Pantisano ist neuer Co-Parteichef neben Ines Schwerdtner
spiegel.description: Die Linke hat eine neue Parteispitze. Ines Schwerdtner wurde wiedergewählt. Luigi Pantisano folgt Jan van Aken mit einem mageren Ergebnis nach. Vor seiner Wahl hatte er noch mit einer Äußerung über die CDU für Aufregung gesorgt.

spiegel.title: Hitzewelle in Deutschland: Hauptsache, einen kühlen Kopf bewahren!
spiegel.description: Brütend heißes Sommerwetter lockt viele Menschen nach draußen. Um sich an Seen oder im Schwimmbad abzukühlen – und um eine Stimmung aufzusaugen, nach der man sich monatelang gesehnt hat.

spiegel.title: König Charles III.: Sieht er die Kinder von Harry und Meghan das erste Mal nach vier Jahren wieder?
spiegel.description: Archie und Lilibet sollen ihren Opa, den britischen König Charles III., das letzte Mal 2022 gesehen haben. Nun begleiten sie Harry und Meghan Berichten zufolge auf einer Reise nach Großbritannien.

spiegel.title: Felix Banaszak Grünen-Co-Chef attackiert Merz mit derben Worten
spiegel.description: »Niemand glaubt mehr daran, dass sich etwas ändert«: Der Grünenpolitiker Felix Banaszak hat Friedrich Merz ungewohnt scharf angegriffen. Dieser habe nicht nur ein Kommunikationsproblem, sondern die falsche Haltung.

spiegel.title: Ronaldinho: Plant er sein Comeback bei einem italienischen Drittligisten?
spiegel.description: Dass italienische Vereine gern ältere Fußballstars verpflichten, ist bekannt. Nun sorgt ein möglicher Transfer des 46-jährigen Ronaldinho zu Ravenna FC für Furore. Dabei ist nicht mal klar, ob er auch spielen wird.

spiegel.title: Wetterwarnung: Hitze, Gewitter und Sturm – Deutschland steckt im Wetter-Schwitzkasten
spiegel.description: Wer am Samstagabend zum Public Viewing möchte, sollte eine Regenjacke parat haben – denn in Teilen des Landes wird es stürmisch. Der Deutsche Wetterdienst warnt vor hohen Temperaturen, Hagel und Sturmböen.

spiegel.title: Friedrich Merz und Julian Nagelsmann: Kanzler und Bundestrainer sind sich fremd
spiegel.description: Kanzler Merz hat dem Bundestrainer und seinem Team alles Gute gewünscht – aber der CDU-Mann und Nagelsmann sind sich fremd. Wie anders war das früher, vor allem zwischen Helmut Kohl und Berti Vogts. Eine nostalgische Erinnerung.

spiegel.title: Colorado River: Die »Megadürre« trocknet Amerikas Südwesten aus
spiegel.description: Rund um den Colorado River, Lebensader für 40 Millionen Menschen, sorgt die Wasserknappheit für Verteilungskämpfe. In einer Stadt in Arizona kommt vielleicht schon im August nichts mehr aus dem Hahn.

spiegel.title: Bolivien: Präsident verhängt Ausnahmezustand nach wochenlangen Protesten
spiegel.description: Seit mehr als sieben Wochen lähmen Straßenblockaden das Land, Millionen Menschen waren von der Außenwelt abgeschnitten. Nun plant Rodrigo Paz Pereira mithilfe des Militärs durchzugreifen.

spiegel.title: Frank Stronach: 93-jähriger Milliardär wegen sexueller Übergriffe schuldig gesprochen
spiegel.description: Der austrokanadische Geschäftsmann und Ex-Politiker Frank Stronach wurde wegen eines »unsittlichen Übergriffs« und sexueller Nötigung schuldig gesprochen. Die vorgeworfenen Taten reichen bis ins Jahr 1977 zurück.

spiegel.title: İlkay Gündoğan - Kolumne zur Fußball-WM 2026: Reizfigur? Ihr tut Leroy Sané unrecht!
spiegel.description: In Folge zwei seiner SPIEGEL-WM-Kolumne schreibt der frühere Nationalelfkapitän İlkay Gündoğan über die Kritik am Offensivspieler, mentale Hürden, und er verrät, wie Sané wirklich ist.

spiegel.title: Chempark Dormagen: 25 Mitarbeiter durch giftige Chemikalie verletzt

spiegel.description: Hat Ihr Vermieter schon Wärmemessgeräte installiert, die den Verbrauch per Funk übertragen? Die Kosten muss meist der Mieter tragen. Es gibt aber Ausnahmen.

undark.title: Interview: California Lawmaker Calls for a Peptide Working Group

undark.title: Making Sense of Data From Wearable Health Trackers
undark.description: Wearable health devices such as smartwatches, glucose monitors, and sleep trackers are blurring the line between consumer wellness and clinical medicine. One physician argues that validation standards and privacy protections must be established to ensure the usefulness of the data these devices generate.

undark.title: In California, a Plan to Help Wildlife Cross a Busy Freeway
undark.description: The 101 freeway in California bisects a mountainous region where threatened cougars and other animals are blocked without a viable path across 10 lanes of heavily trafficked roadway. But an ambitious 210-foot “vegetated bridge” will soon be home to what organizers say is the largest wildlife crossing anywhere in the world.

undark.title: Promising ‘Liquid Biopsies’ May Not Be Ready for Primetime
undark.description: Multi-cancer early detection tests seek to spot cancer from a single blood draw. Enabling earlier cancer diagnoses could help save lives and limit the need for invasive interventions. But while the tests are promising, physicians have expressed doubt about routine use by low-risk and asymptomatic individuals.

undark.title: Book Review: How Radio Astronomy Made the Invisible Visible
undark.description: According to astronomer Emma Chapman’s revelatory “The Echoing Universe,” the history of radio astronomy is filled with surprises that have revealed parts of the universe that would otherwise remain hidden and invisible — DIY instruments, secrets accidentally uncovered, and persistent connections to Earth.

undark.title: Risk Aversion in Science Stifles Innovation
undark.description: Does the scientific enterprise play it too safe? C. Brandon Ogbunu argues that risk-taking in science involves a willingness to reflect on the processes and incentives of the profession — and to dramatically overhaul them if they do not work. Only then can true scientific innovation take shape.

undark.title: A Peptide, a Secretive Scientist, and a Debate Over Evidence
undark.description: Access to unapproved peptides like BPC-157 has become a cause célèbre for the MAHA movement. Undark contributing editor Sara Talpos digs into the untold history of BPC-157 and its long journey from the scientific margins to the center of a debate over U.S. drug regulation.

undark.title: Book Review: Within Our Cells, the Miracle of Constant Mutation
undark.description: Our cells are constantly mutating in a battle for the survival of the fittest that is raging inside us daily, Roxanne Khamsi writes in “Beyond Inheritance.” Many of these mutations are harmless, others are cellular deviants that lead to disease, and remarkably, some can actually self-correct.

undark.title: The Six-Week Postpartum Checkup Comes Too Late
undark.description: In the U.S., maternity care generally ends with a checkup scheduled six weeks after giving birth. This single doctor’s appointment may be efficient for billing and discharge protocols, but the timing reflects the structure of the health care system more than the reality of maternal recovery.

undark.title: Book Review:  The Case for Making Data-Driven Decisions
undark.description: In “Beyond Belief: How Evidence Shows What Really Works,” science journalist Helen Pearson profiles a group of people working in medicine and other fields who became leaders of the worldwide evidence movement, which encourages the use of data from rigorous research to direct treatments, policies, and plans.

proj-syn.title: How (Not) to Conserve Tropical Forests
proj-syn.description: Although the Tropical Forest Forever Facility that emerged from the last United Nations Climate Conference is unlikely to succeed, critically important global conservation efforts are not doomed. Through sustainability-linked sovereign bonds and loans, tropical countries can overcome the TFFF’s fatal flaws.

proj-syn.title: Was Brexit Inevitable?
proj-syn.description: If counterfactual history is motivated by a refusal to accept what many have deemed inevitable, it is newly relevant now that the West is marking the tenth anniversary of the Brexit referendum. Even if Britain's fateful choice was caused by deeper structural and historical forces, that does not justify fatalism.

proj-syn.title: Questioning the Just War Doctrine
proj-syn.description: With war becoming more frequent and more lethal to civilians, Pope Leo XIV and the College of Cardinals are wading into the debate over its legitimacy. The best outcome of the “consistory” Leo is convening in in late June would be to authorize an overhaul of the just war doctrine for the modern era—and ask the necessary questions.

proj-syn.title: Bosnia Must Stand on Its Own
proj-syn.description: The Trump administration's recent, apparently corrupt intervention in Bosnia and Herzegovina could have been an opportunity finally to put the country on a path to full independence after more than 30 years of being a ward of the international community. Instead, the vicious cycle of dependence looks set to continue.

proj-syn.title: The Strategic Logic of the AI Arms Race
proj-syn.description: AI and drones are rapidly transforming warfare, shifting military power toward countries that can combine manufacturing scale, advanced AI systems, and battlefield data. The United States and Europe, hobbled by political dysfunction and obsolete military structures, remain dangerously unprepared.

proj-syn.title: The Meaning of Limited Government—Then and Now
proj-syn.description: In 1776, Adam Smith and America’s founders envisioned an economy that allowed individuals to pursue their own material well-being, with minimal government intervention. Today, America’s Republican Party claims to be committed to restoring that laissez-faire ideal, even as they make a mockery of its animating principles.

proj-syn.title: AI Sovereignty Is About Options, Not Ownership
proj-syn.description: The US government’s abrupt decision to suspend foreign access to Anthropic’s Fable 5 and Mythos 5 models clarifies what “AI sovereignty” is really about. In the emerging AI economy, competitive advantage will come not from owning a single model, but from being able to evaluate, select, and orchestrate many models.

proj-syn.title: The Promise and Peril of AGI
proj-syn.description: Artificial general intelligence could dramatically increase human prosperity and free people from countless mundane tasks. But unless its benefits and ownership are broadly shared, it could deprive billions of workers of their livelihoods and pave the way for a new form of techno-authoritarianism.

proj-syn.title: Reversing Brexit Is Labour’s Best Hope
proj-syn.description: When it comes to the relationship between the United Kingdom and the European Union, political expediency and economic logic both point in the same direction. A majority of British voters now believe that Brexit was a mistake, and they are looking for a leader who will put the issue back on the national agenda.

proj-syn.title: Global Health Reform Must Bolster Innovation
proj-syn.description: As funding falls for global public health, calls for a country-led system have grown louder. Such reforms are necessary, but they must not come at the expense of new vaccines, medicines, and diagnostics, which can be delivered by strengthening mechanisms—such as product development partnerships—that already work.

proj-syn.title: Learning from the Right Sovereign Wealth Funds
proj-syn.description: The Gulf has made establishing a sovereign wealth fund seem like a strategic—and glamorous—choice, leading countries like Canada to launch their own. But Latin America has run this experiment many times over the years, offering a more realistic view of an SWF’s pitfalls and promise.

proj-syn.title: Europe Cannot Afford Another Lost Year
proj-syn.description: European businesses need simpler rules, faster permitting, affordable energy, stronger infrastructure, and a fully functioning single market. The longer that European policymakers fail to deliver on these policies, the greater Europe’s competitiveness challenge will become.

proj-syn.title: White House Fight Night
proj-syn.description: The venue on the South Lawn for UFC Freedom 250 was built, approved, lit, filmed, defended, watched, and enjoyed as part of a celebration of freedom. President Donald Trump’s chosen object to represent that celebration was a cage.

proj-syn.title: The US-Iran Agreement Is a First Step
proj-syn.description: While the recently announced US-Iranian memorandum of understanding is certainly good news, it is not definitive. The path from a statement of diplomatic intent to a fully restored, non-inflationary energy supply chain is fraught with political, technical, and physical risks.

proj-syn.title: Developing-Country Risk Is Being Mispriced
proj-syn.description: When investors say there are no “bankable” projects in developing economies, they are typically referring less to project quality than to the cost of capital. But the assumptions driving up risk premia are not supported by the evidence, and until this changes, the misallocation of capital will continue to undermine development.

proj-syn.title: The Fed Has Been Honest and Stupid
proj-syn.description: It would be easy—and a mistake—to blame the US Federal Reserve’s many blunders on corrupt bureaucrats or imagined conspiracies. The truth of the matter is that the central bank relies on an outdated regional map and lagging indicators that no longer tell the whole story, while battling macroeconomic blazes that politicians stoke.

proj-syn.title: A New Framework for Climate Displacement
proj-syn.description: Global warming is already uprooting communities and impoverishing people who remain in vulnerable areas—a crisis that is often overshadowed by the focus on decarbonization. But the Global Climate Mobility Principles offer policymakers a framework for ensuring that these individuals maintain their agency and rights.

proj-syn.title: Peace With Iran Is All About Lebanon Now
proj-syn.description: US President Donald Trump says that he "calls the shots" on negotiating with Iran, and Israel has no choice but to submit to a deal that undermines its security interests. But a deal that makes Trump the protector of Lebanon—and, by extension, Iran-backed Hezbollah—could put the US and Israel on a collision course.
